question.primary_nl: Which seller IDs were associated with more than 10 distinct orders placed in 2017, with every one of those orders having at least one review and all associated reviews scoring 5?
nl_variants: Find sellers with more than ten 2017 orders, requiring a review on every such order and no review score other than 5.
For each seller, count distinct 2017 orders and require more than 10; every order must have a review and the minimum score across all its reviews must be 5.

evidence.golden_sql:
WITH seller_orders AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT oi.seller_id, o.order_id
    FROM olist_order_items_dataset oi JOIN olist_orders_dataset o ON oi.order_id=o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01'
), reviewed_orders AS (
    SELECT order_id, MIN(review_score) AS minimum_score
    FROM olist_order_reviews_dataset GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT so.seller_id
FROM seller_orders so LEFT JOIN reviewed_orders r ON r.order_id=so.order_id
GROUP BY so.seller_id
HAVING COUNT(*)>10 AND COUNT(r.order_id)=COUNT(*) AND MIN(r.minimum_score)=5;
evidence.reasoning_steps: Deduplicate seller-order pairs for 2017 purchases. Aggregate reviews per order and left join them so unreviewed orders remain visible. Require more than ten orders, a review aggregate on every order, and minimum review score 5.

question.primary_nl: Identify the top 5 customer cities with the highest average freight value per order item on orders placed in 2018, considering only cities with at least 10 distinct orders placed in that year.
nl_variants: Which five customer cities had the highest average item freight for 2018 purchases, among cities with at least ten distinct 2018 orders?
Count all 2018 orders by customer city and require at least ten; rank qualifying cities by AVG(item freight_value) for their 2018 purchases and return the top five.
Top five customer cities by average freight per item for 2018 orders, with at least ten distinct 2018 orders per city?

evidence.golden_sql:
WITH eligible_locations AS (
    SELECT c.customer_city
    FROM olist_orders_dataset o JOIN olist_customers_dataset c ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id
    WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2019-01-01'
    GROUP BY c.customer_city HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10
)
SELECT c.customer_city, AVG(oi.freight_value) AS avg_freight
FROM olist_orders_dataset o JOIN olist_customers_dataset c ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id
JOIN olist_order_items_dataset oi ON oi.order_id=o.order_id
JOIN eligible_locations e ON e.customer_city=c.customer_city
WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2019-01-01'
GROUP BY c.customer_city ORDER BY avg_freight DESC LIMIT 5;
evidence.reasoning_steps: Count all orders purchased in 2018 by customer_city, including orders without items, and require at least 10. Join qualifying locations to 2018 purchased items and compute AVG(oi.freight_value) by location. Sort by average freight descending and return five cities.

question.primary_nl: Calculate the total freight value for 2018 orders, grouped by customer state, but only include states that had more than 100 orders placed in that year.
nl_variants: For states with over 100 orders in 2018, what was the total shipping cost per state?
First count all 2018 orders by customer state and require more than 100; then sum item freight_value for 2018 purchases in each eligible state.
Total 2018 freight grouped by customer state (min 101 orders)?

evidence.golden_sql:
WITH eligible_locations AS (
    SELECT c.customer_state
    FROM olist_orders_dataset o JOIN olist_customers_dataset c ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id
    WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2019-01-01'
    GROUP BY c.customer_state HAVING COUNT(*) >= 101
)
SELECT c.customer_state, SUM(oi.freight_value) AS total_freight
FROM olist_orders_dataset o JOIN olist_customers_dataset c ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id
JOIN olist_order_items_dataset oi ON oi.order_id=o.order_id
JOIN eligible_locations e ON e.customer_state=c.customer_state
WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2019-01-01'
GROUP BY c.customer_state;
evidence.reasoning_steps: Count all orders purchased in 2018 by customer_state, including orders without items, and require at least 101. Join qualifying locations to 2018 purchased items and compute SUM(oi.freight_value) by location.

question.primary_nl: Calculate the average freight value per order item, grouped by customer city, for orders placed in 2018; include only cities with more than 50 distinct orders placed in that year.
nl_variants: For 2018 purchases, average item freight by customer city, keeping cities with more than 50 distinct orders placed in 2018.
First count all 2018 orders by customer city and require more than 50; then calculate AVG(freight_value) across the 2018 item rows in each eligible city.
Average item freight for cities with at least 51 distinct orders placed in 2018?

evidence.golden_sql:
WITH eligible_locations AS (
    SELECT c.customer_city
    FROM olist_orders_dataset o JOIN olist_customers_dataset c ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id
    WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2019-01-01'
    GROUP BY c.customer_city HAVING COUNT(*) >= 51
)
SELECT c.customer_city, AVG(oi.freight_value) AS avg_freight
FROM olist_orders_dataset o JOIN olist_customers_dataset c ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id
JOIN olist_order_items_dataset oi ON oi.order_id=o.order_id
JOIN eligible_locations e ON e.customer_city=c.customer_city
WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2019-01-01'
GROUP BY c.customer_city;
evidence.reasoning_steps: Count all orders purchased in 2018 by customer_city, including orders without items, and require at least 51. Join qualifying locations to 2018 purchased items and compute AVG(oi.freight_value) by location.

question.primary_nl: Identify the top 3 English product categories with the highest average review score for orders placed in the first half of 2018, considering only categories associated with at least 20 review records.

evidence.golden_sql:
WITH category_reviews AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT t.product_category_name_english, r.review_id, r.order_id, r.review_score
    FROM olist_order_reviews_dataset r
    JOIN olist_orders_dataset o ON r.order_id = o.order_id
    JOIN olist_order_items_dataset oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN olist_products_dataset p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
    JOIN product_category_name_translation t ON p.product_category_name = t.product_category_name
    WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01 00:00:00'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-07-01 00:00:00'
)
SELECT product_category_name_english, AVG(review_score) AS avg_score
FROM category_reviews
GROUP BY product_category_name_english
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
ORDER BY avg_score DESC
LIMIT 3;
